title: Pauri 3, sound: gaavai ko taan
hook: gaavai ko taan hovai kisai taan

segments.voice: Yesterday, haumai, the I that fills the picture. Your line was all within the order. Did you catch one I and add who else was there? Day one hundred sixty-seven.

A crowded room, and everyone is singing, but not the same song. One person sings about how strong someone is. Another about their generosity. Another about how far away they seem, and another about how close. It could be chaos. Instead, it sounds like a choir that has agreed on one thing: whoever they're singing about is worth singing about. That's the third pauri of Japji. Its first two words are the whole idea: someone sings.
screen: `A ROOM FULL OF SINGERS.` → `EVERYONE A DIFFERENT SONG.` → `SOMEONE SINGS.`

segments.voice: The opening line: gaavai ko taan, hovai kisai taan. Let's sound it. Gaavai: GAA-vai. It means sings. Ko: short and round, ko. Someone. Gaavai ko: someone sings. Taan: a long aa, and the n at the end is made with the tongue curled back a little. It means power, strength. Hovai: HO-vai, if there is, if one has. Kisai: KI-sai, to anyone. So the line says, roughly: someone sings of the power, if anyone has the power to sing it. Tomorrow, the meaning. Today, the build. Gaavai ko starts line after line, like hukmee did in the second pauri. Gaavai ko daat jaanai neesaan: someone sings of the gifts. Gaavai ko gun vadiaaeeaa chaar: someone sings of the virtues and the greatness. Gaavai ko, gaavai ko, gaavai ko, until the room is full. Some of the lines swing between opposites: someone sings that He seems far away; someone sings that He's right here, face to face. And then the pauri lifts up out of the list with a new sound: kathnaa kathee na aavai tot. Kathnaa, kathee: telling, told. There's no end to the telling. Millions and millions tell it, the pauri says, and the telling never runs out. The last line ends with a word worth listening for, the sound of someone free of every worry: veparvaahu. We'll unpack it tomorrow. For now, notice the rhythm: gaavai ko, someone sings, again and again, like voices joining a chorus one by one.
screen: `GAAVAI — SINGS. KO — SOMEONE.` · `TAAN — POWER, STRENGTH.` · `GAAVAI KO, AGAIN AND AGAIN.` · `NO END TO THE TELLING.` · then, large: `PAURI THREE.`

segments.voice: Hum first. No words, just a low hum on one note for a breath or two. Then put the words on it: gaavai ko taan, hovai kisai taan. Again, a little slower, and if a tune wants to come, let it; this pauri is about singing. Once more, softly. Then stop, and listen to the silence after, as if the room of singers has just gone quiet. If you pray, you can rest in Waheguru. The bell holds the time.
Taan. Power, strength: what someone sings of, gaavai ko taan, line after line in this pauri.
Your line: gaavai ko. Today, notice someone singing, humming or whistling, on the street, in a shop, in your house, and let yourself enjoy it. Day one hundred sixty-seven.

howItsDone: The third pauri of Japji is recited each morning; its repeated gaavai ko, someone sings, is often a favorite for learners because the rhythm is easy to catch.

fork.setup: in pauri three, singers disagree: some say He seems far away. what do others sing?
options: that He is right here, face to face.
that no one should sing at all.
fork.reveal: some sing far away, some sing present, face to face; the pauri holds both.

original.script: ਗਾਵੈ ਕੋ ਤਾਣੁ ਹੋਵੈ ਕਿਸੈ ਤਾਣੁ
original.say: GAA-vai ko TAAN, HO-vai KI-sai TAAN
original.note: Gurmukhi: the opening line of Japji's third pauri. the n in taan is retroflex, tongue curled back.

trapdoor: what you thought: a line about singing.
what it means: someone sings of the power, if anyone has the power; the pauri fills with different singers.
what a scholar hears: the final ਣ in taan is a retroflex n; gaavai ko is repeated as an anaphora, like hukmee in pauri two.

notes: Romanized lines (gaavai ko daat jaanai neesaan; gaavai ko gun vadiaaeeaa chaar; kathnaa kathee na aavai tot) and their short paraphrases: confirm.
